wait_for_latching.evidence: A token signaled with -S, then left with NO waiter alive for 3s, was still consumed by a later wait (latch_rc=0). That is exactly the inter-wait gap Task 10's bounded re-wait must survive.
wait_for_latching.one_shot: A second wait on the same token timed out (rewait_rc=1): the latch is consumed by the first SUCCESSFUL wait. This is what makes Task 10 safe -- a first wait that TIMED OUT cannot have consumed the token.
wait_for_latching.gap_probe_caveat: The plan's second probe corroborates nothing. Its signal fires at t~2s while the second wait (--timeout 10, started at t~1s) is ALREADY blocking, so second_rc=0 only proves a live waiter receives a signal. latching is derived from the first probe alone.

rc_confirmation_screen.rc_anchor_rationale: The sent line is literally '/rc'. The composer EXPANDS the alias, so the submitted-command line reads '/remote-control' -- bare '/remote-control' occurs twice (echo + response). '/remote-control is active' occurs ONCE, only in the response region, and cannot appear in the sent line.
rc_confirmation_screen.rename_anchor_rationale: The naive anchor (the title text itself) matches 3 lines INCLUDING the command echo -- the exact 'shell echo defeating composer verify' defeat. 'Session renamed to:' matches exactly 1 line and cannot appear in the sent line unless the title itself were that string.
rc_confirmation_screen.addendum_3_result: NEGATIVE -- the hazard did not reproduce. 'send' still landed after /remote-control was active: the /rename sent AFTER /rc was accepted and confirmed. Operator addendum #3 (N=1, unproven) is not supported here.

ref_resolution_scoping.finding: rename-tab and close-surface resolve surface/tab refs WITHIN THE CALLER'S WORKSPACE unless --workspace is passed; send, send-key and read-screen resolve them cross-workspace with a bare --surface.
ref_resolution_scoping.impact: Breaks the workspace-fallback path, where the successor surface is by definition NOT in the caller's workspace. Module 3 must always pass --workspace to rename-tab and close-surface.

evidence.cross_workspace_close_with_flag: OK surface:80 workspace:29 (exit 0), target was surface:77

ref_resolution_scoping.warmth_irrelevant: The bare cross-workspace rename failed identically on a COLD and a WARM surface, so this is ref scoping, not lazy terminal instantiation.
